stories.title: Supreme Court Dismisses Centre's Challenge To War Injury Pension To Soldier Posted In Kargil
stories.summary: The Court also asked the Union to clear the ambiguities in the pension rules.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Court also asked the Union to clear the ambiguities in the pension rules.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 28) has upheld the grant of a War Injury pension to ex-armed forces personnel for the ailment which developed owing to his posting at Kargil as part of Operation Rakshak.

A bench of Justice Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe dismissed the Union government's appeal against the High Court's and Armed Forces Tribunal's order which granted a War Injury pension to the ex-personnel in place of the disability pension.

At the same time, the Court also suggested that the government issue a comprehensive and clearly identifiable subordinate legislation governing the services of ex-personnel who became eligible for a War Injury Pension, noting that there is uncertainty about which Rules, Regulations, Instructions and Policies of the Ministry of Defence (MoD) are applicable.
“We continue to wonder why this uncertainty about applicable rules continues.
It is high time that the MoD issues a comprehensive and clearly identifiable subordinate legislation governing the services.
This is necessary for fairness in action and also for good governance.”, the Court said.
The respondent Narender Kumar joined the Indian Army in December 1996 and was posted at Kargil from July 2003 to July 2005.
During this posting, he was diagnosed with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis in January 2005.
He was subsequently diagnosed with two spinal conditions while posted in West Bengal.
When he was discharged from service in January 2013, the Release Medical Board assessed his disabilities as aggravated by military service at 70%, rounded off to 75% for life.
He was granted disability pension comprising service and disability elements.

stories.title: Cyclone Arnab: Guntur district records 41 mm average rainfall; authorities stay alert

article_sentences: Guntur district recorded an average rainfall of 41 mm as on 9 a.m., Wednesday, with Duggirala mandal receiving the highest rainfall of 77.8 mm, followed by Tadepalle at 71.2 mm and Chebrole at 70 mm, amid the impact of cyclone Arnab.

According to the daily rainfall statistics, Mangalagiri and Kollipara received 66.6 mm each, Tenali 63.8 mm, Pedakakani 50.8 mm, Guntur East 38.4 mm, Guntur West 38.2 mm, Tadikonda 36 mm, Thullur 31.8 mm, Ponnur 24.5 mm, Kakumanu 21.6 mm, Medikonduru 18.6 mm, Vatticherukuru 17.4 mm, Pedanandipadu 16.2 mm, Prathipadu 15.6 mm and Phirangipuram 12.4 mm.
District Collector C.M. Saikanth Varma directed officials to remain at the field level and maintain heightened vigilance throughout Wednesday in view of the cyclone and continuing rainfall.

During a teleconference with officials, the Collector instructed them to inspect low-lying areas, assess the situation and ensure uninterrupted road connectivity, noting that strong winds were prevailing and stressing the need for prompt action to address emerging problems.

Stating that a tree that had fallen at Emani village in Duggirala mandal had been removed, Mr. Varma instructed Roads and Buildings and Panchayat Raj engineers to continuously monitor road conditions and take immediate remedial measures.
Water Resources Department engineers were directed to monitor water flows at Prakasam Barrage and other channels.
Schools and colleges in the district were declared closed for the day as a precautionary measure.
The Collector said Yanadi families had already been shifted to rehabilitation centres.
He instructed officials to provide quality food to the families and milk to children.
He directed all departments to submit regular situation reports and remain fully alert throughout the day.
He also cautioned people against venturing near streams, rivulets, tanks and rivers during the adverse weather conditions.

stories.title: Cyclone Arnab claims five lives in Andhra Pradesh; Naidu announces relief package
stories.summary: ₹5 lakh ex gratia for each victim; aid announced for farmers, fishermen, households and businesses
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Arnab claimed five lives in Andhra Pradesh, prompting Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu to announce a comprehensive relief and compensation package for affected families, farmers, fishermen and businesses.
Expressing condolences to the bereaved families, he said the government had made extensive efforts to minimise casualties and property damage.

Addressing a press conference at the Secretariat on Wednesday, the Chief Minister identified the deceased as Amrapinni Devmud and Kolamuru Madhavi from the Visakhapatnam region, Chukkala Kishore from Bhimavaram, Bhagyalakshmi from Anakapalli and Kollu Venkayamma from Sakretipalli.
Mr. Devmud died after a tree fell on an electric wire, while Ms. Madhavi died after an electric pole fell on her.
Mr. Kishore was killed when a palm tree fell on him, and Ms. Bhagyalakshmi died of electrocution.
Ms. Venkayamma died when a wall collapsed on her while she was travelling in a passenger vehicle.
The families of each deceased person would receive an ex gratia payment of ₹5 lakh, Mr. Naidu said.
He urged people to remain cautious even after the cyclone crossed the coast.
Families whose houses were inundated would receive 25 kg of rice, while fishermen’s families and handloom households would get 50 kg.
Each affected family would also receive one kg each of red gram, onions, sugar and potatoes, besides one litre of palm oil.
Those staying in relief camps would receive ₹1,000 per person, subject to a ceiling of ₹3,000 per family.
Partially damaged houses would receive ₹10,000 in compensation.

article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission (SEC) has postponed polling for the Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) and Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) elections from November 3 to November 5 because the counting of votes for the urban local body (ULB) elections is to be done on November 3 under the revised schedule.

In a press release on Wednesday (October 28, 2026), State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha said that after an assessment of the situation created by Cyclone Arnab, and on the basis of assurances given by the Collectors and District Election.
Authorities of the cyclone-affected districts, it was decided not to change the November 1 polling date for the ULBs.

Since the available police and polling personnel were not enough to manage both the counting of votes for the ULB elections and the polling for MPTCs and ZPTCs on November 3, it has been decided to defer the MPTC and ZPTC polls to November 5.

Mr. Punetha said the ULB elections had to be postponed from October 28 to November 1 in compliance with the orders of the Supreme Court, which was acting on writ petitions filed by the YSR Congress Party.
That moved the ULB counting to November 3, the day originally fixed for the MPTC and ZPTC polls.

Under the revised schedule, polling for MPTCs and ZPTCs will be held on November 5 and any repolling on November 6, both from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. The counting of votes will be taken up on November 7, and results declared upon its completion.
Under the original schedule, the votes were to be counted on November 5.
Mr. Punetha had said on Monday that the Commission would take a decision on the ULB polls only if the cyclone proved devastating.

In his letter, Naidu highlighted damage to crops, houses, roads and electricity poles caused by the cyclone and urged the Centre to dispatch assessment teams at the earliest, according to a press release.
Around 16 National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and 11 State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams have been deployed across 14 districts for rescue and relief operations.
More than 28,000 people have been shifted to rehabilitation centres in cyclone-affected areas.
Konaseema, Kakinada, East Godavari, West Godavari, Anakapalli and Krishna are among the districts severely affected by the cyclone, the Chief Minister said.
Control rooms and the State Emergency Operations Centre are functioning round the clock to coordinate the response.
The government is prioritising relief operations and the restoration of electricity and drinking water supplies in affected areas.
Naidu said a comprehensive report on the damage would be submitted to the Centre after a detailed assessment.
He also urged the Union government to continue providing support through the NDRF and other central agencies for relief and rehabilitation.

Earlier on Wednesday, Naidu held a teleconference with around 32,000 personnel, including district collectors and field-level staff, to review the cyclone's impact and the relief and restoration measures being undertaken across the state.
He also held a review meeting with senior officials to assess crop damage and directed them to prepare preliminary estimates.

article_sentences: NEW DELHI: Cyclone ‘Arnab’ has battered India’s eastern coast, uprooting trees and electric poles, damaging roads and bringing torrential rain, with some areas of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha recording up to 30 cm of rainfall.
The storm’s impact is now expected to extend to Nepal, which is bracing for several days of rain, thunderstorms and snowfall from Thursday.

The Nepal Meteorological Department’s Weather Forecasting Division said the country was currently experiencing the partial influence of westerly winds, with the approaching cyclone expected to bring widespread precipitation and a risk of heavy rain and snowfall through the weekend.
“The country is currently under the partial influence of westerly winds.
In addition, the country is expected to come under the influence of Cyclone ‘Arnab’, developed over the Bay of Bengal, from Kartik 12 (Thursday),” the department said in its latest bulletin.
Weather conditions remained relatively clear in the Himalayan and hilly regions on Wednesday morning, although fog and mist affected parts of the Terai, valleys and river basins.
The department forecast increasing cloud cover and scattered precipitation from Wednesday afternoon, with conditions becoming more unsettled overnight.
Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini provinces are among the areas expected to experience rain, while snowfall is possible in Himalayan regions.
The risk is forecast to increase on Thursday night, when thunderstorms and lightning could accompany rain and snowfall.
Heavy precipitation is possible in parts of Koshi, Bagmati and Gandaki provinces, while some areas of Lumbini could also receive heavy rainfall.
Friday and Saturday are expected to bring the most widespread impacts.
The department warned that heavy rain or snowfall could affect several provinces, with isolated locations facing the possibility of very heavy precipitation.

stories.headline: Israelis await final election results as Netanyahu rivals weigh joining forces with Arab parties
stories.title: Israelis await final election results as Netanyahu rivals weigh joining forces with Arab parties
stories.summary: Jerusalem, Oct 28: Anxious Israelis watched election results near completion Wednesday after the highest voter turnout in over a quarter-century, as no clear winner emerged and weeks of negotiating could lie ahead for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and an array of opposition parties trying to unseat him. Arab-led parties made a historic showing, but it's not clear if other opponents of Netanyahu's far-right government would form a coalition with them for a majority of seats in parliament. Issues around the Palestinians and their descendants remain incredibly sensitive in Israel. Netanyahu seeks to remain the country's longest-serving prime minister. In defiant comments after the vote, he dismissed the idea of partnering with Arab parties — whose constituents make up 20 per cent of Israel's population — as treasonous. On Wednesday, Netanyahu warned against a “dangerous government” that might include them. He won't work with the Arab-led parties, and they have ruled that out, too. His top challenger, centrist former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, has left the door open to partnering with Arab parties under certain conditions, including their recognition of Israel as a Jewish state and of Hamas as an extremist group. But it's not clear whether some of Eisenkot's likely partners who have ruled out such an alliance will change their minds to force Netanyahu from office. Israeli voters choose parties, not individuals. With 85 per cent of votes counted, Netanyahu's Likud party has 20.8 per cent and Eisenkot's Yashar party has 16.1 per cent. The official count does not indicate how many seats each will have in parliament, the 120-seat Knesset. Emerging results indicated that neither Netanyahu's nor Eisenkot's coalition blocs would reach the 61 seats needed for a majority. Likud's vote share declined from 23.4 per cent in the previous election in 2022. Netanyahu faces a setback but not outright defeat Nearly 78 per cent of eligible voters turned out, the highest since 1999. Final results are expected in the coming days, including from hundreds of thousands of absentee ballots yet to be counted from military personnel and diplomats. Voting reflected unease over Netanyahu's alliance with the far-right and anger in a war-weary nation over military draft exemptions for the significant ultra-Orthodox Jewish population. But results suggest opponents were unable to capitalise on the grief caused by the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attack to decisively push him from office. One partner losing support, however, was far-right national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. For many Israelis, he represented the worst strain of Netanyahu's government, openly taunting Palestinian detainees and asserting that many in Gaza are “not even people.” Vote-counting suggested Likud would remain the largest party and best placed to be tapped to form a government by Israel's president, Isaac Herzog. The president, however, isn't required to task the leader of the party holding the most seats. “We must do everything we can, certainly after yesterday, to avoid another round of elections,” Herzog said Wednesday. The most obvious path to a parliamentary majority could involve Eisenkot partnering with Arab-led parties — which have 14.9 per cent of the votes counted — but that's politically challenging. In a speech early Wednesday that focused on national unity, Eisenkot pledged to form a government and promised “a new era — an era of hope." If no one can put together a majority coalition, new elections could be held early next year. Israel held five elections between April 2019 and November 2022 because of a similar stalemate. Whether thousands of Israelis living abroad would again fly back home to vote, and whether Arab voters would again surge to the polls, is unclear. Minority governments also are possible, but they must rely on cooperation from parties outside the government to pass legislation. Arab-led parties could hold the key Confronted with Arab parties' strong election showing, Israelis have renewed a debate about identity. “We have no future here if we do not stop being afraid," said Yair Golan, whose Democrats party supports bringing Arab-led parties into a coalition. "We must no longer accept Netanyahu's racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes.” Israel's Arab citizens are descendants of Palestinians who remained in the state after its creation in 1948. They often face discrimination and are viewed with wariness because of their solidarity with the Palestinian cause. That suspicion intensified after October 7, even though Arab citizens were also among those killed and abducted. The mood was joyful overnight at the headquarters of the United Arab List, the lone Arab party to ever join a governing coalition, briefly, in 2021. “We are here, we are not on the sidelines,” party leader Mansour Abbas declared. Some Israelis found that an unusual, if not uncomfortable, prospect. “We are little by little coming to a situation where we have to face reality," said Hanna Doukhan, a voter in Tel Aviv. "I don't see a possibility to form a government without the Arabs.” Others were hopeful. “This would open the door to repairing our society" while preserving Israel as the national home of the Jewish people, said Eti Wissotzky-Cohen in Tel Aviv. And in Nazareth, one of Israel's largest Arab cities, Awni Zoabi thanked God for a possible return to rationality in a country where extreme rhetoric has increased. “The Arabic language has become as if it were a crime," Zoabi said. Attitudes over Netanyahu will shape the days ahead Netanyahu has had a nearly unbroken 17-year rule. Israelis were divided over him even before the deadliest attack in the country's history. The resulting wars, along with settler violence in the occupied West Bank, have stoked worldwide outrage, straining ties with Israel's closest allies and fueling a rise in antisemitism. Netanyahu's supporters believe he is protecting Israel's security and Jewish identity in the face of international pressure and liberal elites at home. “I prefer that (Netanyahu) assembles the coalition,” said Ran Cohen, a Jerusalem resident. “He's the only one who knows how to do the job properly, knows how to speak to the world.” Detractors say Netanyahu, facing an ongoing corruption trial, dragged out the war in Gaza and its hostage crisis for political reasons. They say he is undermining Israel's independent judiciary. And they accuse his government of allowing ultra-Orthodox religious Jews to avoid military conscription. Eisenkot is viewed by supporters as a capable leader with sterling security credentials. His son and two nephews were killed in Gaza, and his backers believe that he feels deeply the country's pain. Parties that likely would partner with him have vowed to improve Israel's international standing and work to conscript ultra-Orthodox men while bolstering the independence of the judiciary.

article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh SEC reschedules MPTC and ZPTC elections, shifting polling to November 5 and counting to November 7 due to staff shortages and overlapping municipal election duties.
Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission (SEC) has announced the decision to reschedul polling and counting for the MPTC and ZPTC elections, amid the shortage of police personnel and polling staff.
The polling, which is supposed to be held on 3 November, will now be held on 5 November from 7am to 5pm.
Re-polling, if required, will be held on 6 November.
Meanwhile, counting has been postponed from 5 November to 7 November and will begin at 8am, with results to be declared as soon as counting is complete.
The changes were made because the counting of municipal election votes coincides with Parishad election polling.
The SEC said the revised schedule would help ensure staff and other resources are used efficiently.
State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha also announced that voting at 88 polling stations in Alluri Sitarama Raju and Polavaram districts will end at 3pm.

Suri Payala has contended that records obtained from the Legislative Department show that the material placed before the Search Committee and the Selection Committee consisted primarily of lists of candidates, service particulars, dates and service records.
According to him, the records do not disclose any specific assessment of the candidates' integrity or experience in election management and conduct.

The petitioner has challenged the appointments made in March 2024 and February 2025 under the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.

The petitioner contends that Section 5 of the 2023 Act requires the Search Committee to prepare a panel of five persons eligible for appointment as Election Commissioners, while Section 6 governs the Selection Committee's recommendation.
He argues that the records do not show a specific assessment of whether the candidates possessed experience in the conduct of elections or satisfied the requirement relating to integrity.
According to the application, the minutes of the selection process refer to candidates being considered on the basis of their eligibility and experience.
However, the petitioner alleges that the underlying records do not disclose any specific exercise to ascertain their election-related experience or integrity.
He further contends that merely recording that Section 5 was noted, without disclosing how its requirements were assessed, does not demonstrate compliance with the statutory framework.

With respect to the appointments of Gyanesh Kumar and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu as ECs made on March 14, 2024, the petitioner has questioned the process through which the Search Committee shortlisted candidates for two vacancies.

stories.headline: From JLR to Iveco, Tata Motors’ high-stakes acquisition strategy
stories.title: From JLR to Iveco, Tata Motors’ high-stakes acquisition strategy
stories.summary: Tata Motors has often looked abroad, buying foreign businesses to acquire technology, expand to new markets and accelerate ambitions that would take years to achieve at home. The track record, however, has been mixed.In 2004, it bought South Korea’s Daewoo Commercial Vehicle for about $102 million, gaining a foothold in a market where building a comparable business from scratch could have taken years, if not decades.Four years later, it made a far bolder move, paying about $2.3 billion to buy Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) from Ford Motor.Now, with its €3.9 billion acquisition of Italy’s Iveco Group, Tata Motors is returning to the familiar playbook: Buy a struggling business, leave its brand and management largely intact, and give it time.“Their acquisitions have been driven by the need to have certain technology where developing it internally could end up costing more time,” says Avik Chattopadhyay, founder of the Indian School for Design of Automobiles (INDEA) at XLRI Delhi-NCR. “It’s also about finding newer ways of doing things, of engineering and even designing your product.”Also Read: Tata Motors takes control of Iveco in €3.9 bn deal, eyes global truck marketTrack RecordTata Motors’ international acquisition strategy gathered momentum in the early 2000s, when it acquired Daewoo. The purchase gave the company access to an established South Korean truck manufacturer, its engineering capabilities and a broader product range.The next move was smaller and shows what happens when the market shrinks. Tata acquired a 21 percent stake in Spanish bus and coach manufacturer Hispano Carrocera in 2005, taking full ownership in 2009. It shut the plant four years later, saying the European bus market had suffered its worst-ever decline after the 2008 crisis.Then came JLR, an acquisition that stunned the auto industry. In 2008, when it bought the storied luxury car maker from Ford, Tata had a fledgling passenger vehicle business at home, which, only years ago, it had wanted to sell to Ford. Acquiring the British luxury car brand gave Tata access to globally recognised brands, established distribution networks, engineering centres and manufacturing facilities. It also gave the Indian company an opportunity to participate in a much higher-value segment of the automotive market.The group’s corporate structure has since changed. Tata Motors used to house its passenger and commercial vehicle (CV) businesses together. They were demerged in October 2025 and are now separately listed companies.The passenger vehicle business, which includes JLR, is now Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd. The CV business that is buying Iveco has been branded as Tata Motors.JLR remains the most closely watched acquisition, not just because of the signal it sent about the company’s global ambitions, but also because of its striking initial turnaround.JLR lost £306 million in its first 10 months under Tata. A decade later, in 2017, it posted a pre-tax profit of £1.6 billion. Capital infusions from Tata, a stream of new models and a manufacturing facility opened in China in FY15 all helped the recovery.“We believe JLR sets a precedent for the successful integration and turnaround of Iveco, considering Iveco’s position and performance in the developed market,” Ambit said in a December 2025 report, pointing to JLR’s early success under Tata Motors as a potential model for Iveco.JLR’s early turnaround, however, proved shortlived. From 2018, the company struggled again, hit by US-China trade tensions, anxiety over Brexit and weak demand for diesel cars in Europe. It has been volatile since, reporting a loss of £244 million after tax in FY26, its first loss since FY23.Also Read: Tata Motors CV turns in profit of Rs1,254 crore; revenue surges 42 percentPlan with IvecoThe Iveco acquisition is different from JLR.JLR gave Tata access to luxury passenger vehicles, globally recognised brands and a higher-margin segment. In CVs, Tata is already a market leader in India with a market share of 36 percent in the first half of FY27. Iveco, which has an 11 percent share of the European Union truck market and is Europe’s second-largest bus manufacturer, is intended to strengthen Tata’s position by expanding in new markets.With Iveco under Tata, the company would become the world’s fourth-largest CV maker by volume. It is expected to have annual sales of over 5,40,000 units and revenues of about €22 billion.An Emkay Global analysis in July 2025 argued that Iveco carried lower execution risk than JLR because the two CV businesses were cash-generative and operated in more stable markets than passenger vehicles.In Iveco, Tata gets access to its advanced technologies, including Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and software-driven vehicles.Tata also gets multiple powertrains including electric, LNG, hybrid and hydrogen for its CV business in existing markets, according to a Crisil Ratings report from August 2025.Cultural differences might be one of the challenges in making the Iveco takeover work, feels XLRI’s Chattopadhyay. “The Europeans have their own pace and their own way of working. Also, when you acquire anything in Europe, you have to work with the existing workforce and unions. European companies come with a lot of caveats.”Back at Bombay House, Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran has set an ambitious target of generating $100 billion in auto revenue by FY31. He has pegged the CV business’s contribution at about $40 billion, a goal he outlined at Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles’ annual meeting this year.Chandrasekaran, who is set to join Iveco’s board as chairperson, will have a direct hand in making sure it comes sooner.

stories.headline: CERC Proposes Allowing Pumped Storage Plants to Participate in High-Price Power Market
stories.title: CERC Proposes Allowing Pumped Storage Plants to Participate in High-Price Power Market
stories.summary: The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) has proposed allowing pumped storage plants (PSPs) to participate in the High Price Day Ahead Market (HP-DAM), potentially providing storage developers with an additional avenue to sell electricity during periods of high demand and prices. In an order, the commission proposed including PSPs as an eligible category of generating stations in the existing HP-DAM segment on power exchanges. The commission has initiated suo motu proceedings on the proposal and invited written submissions from parties within 15 days of the order. The proposal follows recommendations from the National Load Despatch Centre (NLDC) and a suggestion from the Ministry of Power to consider allowing PSPs to participate in the high-price market segment. CERC said the existing Day Ahead Market (DAM) alone may not provide sufficient commercial opportunities for pumped storage projects under prevailing market conditions. Participation in HP-DAM could improve their commercial viability by allowing them to access periods of higher demand and prices. The commission also noted that greater participation by pumped storage plants could improve the utilisation of flexible storage resources during periods of constrained power supply, supporting grid flexibility. India has 7.4 GW of operational pumped storage capacity According to an analysis submitted by NLDC, India had 7,425.6 MW of operational pumped storage capacity, comprising 4,845.6 MW of on-stream projects and 2,580 MW of off-stream projects, based on a Central Electricity Authority (CEA) report published in January 2026. Another 15,870 MW of PSP capacity was under construction, while the country's estimated pumped storage potential stood at approximately 290.2 GW. NLDC noted that operational pumped storage plants were almost fully tied up, leaving limited merchant capacity among operational inter-state transmission system-connected projects. Allowing PSPs with merchant capacity to participate in HP-DAM could provide an additional market for energy arbitrage during periods of high-price discovery. ALSO READ: Australia Walks Away From 7.2 GWh of Pumped Hydro. India Is Planning 100 GW Solar and evening peak prices offer arbitrage opportunity The commission's proposal is supported by NLDC's analysis of market-clearing prices between April 2025 and July 2026, which identified a substantial difference between electricity prices during solar generation hours and evening peak demand. According to the analysis, average unconstrained market-clearing prices in the Day Ahead Market were approximately ₹2.20 per unit during solar hours and ₹6.57 per unit during evening peak hours. The resulting price differential of around ₹4.37 per unit indicates a potential arbitrage opportunity for pumped storage projects, subject to project-specific costs and operating conditions. Pumped storage plants use electricity to pump water to an upper reservoir when power is relatively inexpensive and generate electricity by releasing the stored water when demand and prices are higher. However, NLDC's analysis also highlighted the limited liquidity of the existing HP-DAM segment. Between April 2025 and July 2026, market clearing occurred on 47 days, or 9.65% of the analysis period, and across 965 time blocks, accounting for 2.06% of the period. While HP-DAM recorded higher price discovery than the regular DAM during certain intervals, the commission noted that actual revenue realisation would depend on both the prices discovered and the volume of electricity successfully cleared. Pumped storage costs could affect commercial viability NLDC's assessment also examined the costs associated with pumped storage projects. The levelised fixed-cost component of PSP tariffs was estimated at approximately ₹3.30-4.98 per unit, while the effective landed tariff, including pumping costs, could reach ₹8.92 per unit, depending on project-specific characteristics and operating assumptions. The order cited several examples of approved or discovered tariffs, including ₹6.69 per unit for Greenko's 500 MW/3,000 MWh standalone storage project awarded by NTPC Renewable Energy Ltd in December 2022, based on the effective storage cost under a two charge-discharge cycle operation. These figures indicate that the commercial case for participation in high-price markets will depend on project costs, pumping expenses, market prices and the availability of trading opportunities. CERC initiates proceedings on proposed inclusion HP-DAM was introduced under the Integrated Day Ahead Market framework to provide a trading avenue for generating stations with high generation costs that could face constraints under the prevailing price ceiling in the regular DAM. The eligible categories currently include gas-based generating stations using imported regasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) and naphtha, imported coal-based generating stations using only imported coal, and battery energy storage systems (BESS). The Ministry of Power's guidelines for promoting pumped storage projects, issued in April 2023, had provided for PSPs and other storage projects to participate in all power exchange market segments, including HP-DAM, to take advantage of price differences between peak and off-peak periods. CERC's latest order proposes extending the existing eligibility framework to pumped storage plants. stories.headline: Cabinet approves 3% DA hike for 48.54 lakh central government employees, 68.71 lakh pensioners
stories.title: Cabinet approves 3% DA hike for 48.54 lakh central government employees, 68.71 lakh pensioners
stories.summary: New Delhi [India], October 28 : The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a 3 per cent increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) for Central Government employees and Dearness Relief (DR) for pensioners, effective July 1, 2026, providing relief against rising prices. The move will raise DA and DR rates from the existing 60 per cent to 63 per cent of basic pay and pension, respectively. The increase is expected to benefit approximately 48.54 lakh Central Government employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners across the country. According to the government, the combined annual financial implication of the increase in DA and DR will be Rs 10,016.10 crore, adding to the Centre's expenditure. The additional instalment of DA and DR has been approved in accordance with the accepted formula based on the recommendations of the 7th Central Pay Commission. Dearness Allowance is paid to serving government employees to help offset the impact of inflation on their cost of living. Dearness Relief serves a similar purpose for pensioners, helping them manage the effect of rising prices on their pension income. The revision will be applicable retrospectively from July 1, 2026, meaning eligible employees and pensioners will be entitled to the revised rates from that date. The Cabinet's decision comes as the government continues to adjust inflation-linked benefits for its employees and pensioners through periodic revisions in DA and DR. The increase in these allowances is linked to an established formula and is intended to help protect the purchasing power of government employees and pensioners against price increases. With the latest revision, both serving employees and pensioners will receive an additional three percentage points over the previous rate of 60 per cent of basic pay or pension, respectively. The decision covers Central Government employees and pensioners and will have a combined annual impact of more than Rs 10,000 crore on the government exchequer. (ANI)

stories.title: Delhi SIR: Supreme Court asks ECI to extend deadlines, simplify enrolment
stories.summary: While addressing the ECI in the Delhi SIR case, the top court clarified that it did not judicially review the ‘logical discrepancy’ in the Bihar SIR case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) asked the Election Commission of India (ECI) to extend deadlines for the SIR in Delhi, and to simplify the enrolment process.
The court also observed that Form 6 of special intensive revision of electoral rolls (SIR) is “cast in stone”, and that all forms, including 6, 7 and 8, cannot be changed.
The top court clarified that it did not judicially review the “logical discrepancy” in the Bihar SIR case.
“In West Bengal, the logical discrepancy was allowed to continue as an interim measure.
The constitutionality of the logical discrepancy has not been examined,” said the Bench comprising CJI Surya Kant, J. Joymalya Bagchi and J.V. Mohana during the hearing.
The top court also asked the ECI to “not go for any cut-off dates” for applying for re-inclusion and gave the ECI two weeks to make the necessary changes.
“There is no election now in the national capital,” the Bench added.

The Bench questioned why those who missed filling and submitting enumeration forms are asked to fill Form 6 for fresh voters, noting the difference between voters who are shifting from a constituency and those who are “temporarily moving out”.
The ECI said that exclusions don’t happen at the draft electoral roll stage and agreed to extend the deadline to submit claims, objections, and enrolment forms for the Delhi SIR.
The CJI urged the ECI to reach out to voters and keep submitting Forms 6 and 7, calling for the simplest remedy.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Asks Law Commission To Recommend Measures For Speedy Execution Of Arbitral Awards
stories.title: Supreme Court Asks Law Commission To Recommend Measures For Speedy Execution Of Arbitral Awards
stories.summary: A 24-year delay in the enforcement of an award forced the Court to make the intervention.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: A 24-year delay in the enforcement of an award forced the Court to make the intervention.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 28) requested the Law Commission of India to undertake a focused study of the statutory and procedural framework governing the enforcement and execution of arbitral awards and recommend measures to ensure their timely enforcement.

A bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Aparesh Kumar Singh said that the prolonged execution of arbitral awards undermines the very objective of arbitration as an effective alternative to conventional civil litigation.
The Court observed that even after an award is rendered and survives judicial challenge, the successful party may be forced to undergo another prolonged round of litigation to realise its benefits.

“The promise of arbitration remains unfulfilled if a party, having traversed the arbitral process, is compelled to embark upon another protracted course of litigation to secure the benefit of the award,” the Court observed.
The judgment was passed in an appeal arising from a dispute in an international commercial arbitration between Iraq-based Royal Construction Company Pvt.
and National Projects Construction Corporation concerning the enforcement of an arbitral award rendered in 2002.
More than 24 years after the award, the parties were still litigating over its enforcement.
The Court noted that the efficacy of the arbitration regime cannot be assessed merely by the speed with which an award is rendered or the limited grounds available to challenge it.
It must also be assessed by whether the successful party can realise the fruits of the award within a reasonable time.

It observed that Section 36 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 provides for the enforcement of arbitral awards in the same manner as decrees of courts, thereby relying on the ordinary execution machinery under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

The Court identified several aspects warranting focused scrutiny, including the identification and disclosure of the award-debtor's assets, coordination between different modes of execution, disposal of repetitive or dilatory objections, and the time taken to conclude execution proceedings.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Upholds Bombay High Court Ruling Setting Aside ₹8,415 Crore YES Bank AT-1 Bond Write-Down
stories.title: Supreme Court Upholds Bombay High Court Ruling Setting Aside ₹8,415 Crore YES Bank AT-1 Bond Write-Down
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has dismissed appeals filed by YES Bank Limited, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Union of India, upholding the Bombay High Court's decision setting aside the permanent write-down of YES Bank's Additional Tier-1 (AT-1) bonds worth ₹8,415 crore.

A Bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Augustine George Masih held that the Administrator of YES Bank could not write down the bonds in contravention of the final YES Bank Limited Reconstruction Scheme, 2020, particularly when the provision expressly providing for the write-down had been omitted from the notified scheme.
The dispute arose from the Administrator's decision dated March 14, 2020, to permanently write down the AT-1 bonds following the reconstruction of the bank.
The bonds had been issued in two tranches of ₹3,000 crore and ₹5,415 crore.

The Court observed that the omission of the write-down provision from the final Reconstruction Scheme, considered alongside the deliberative process preceding its notification, indicated that the Central Government had consciously decided not to incorporate such a provision.
The Administrator could not rely on a general savings clause in the scheme to claim specific authority to write down the bonds.
The Court also examined the RBI's Basel III Capital Regulations and the Information Memoranda governing the bonds.
It considered whether the conditions authorising a write-down had been satisfied and whether the Administrator had acted in accordance with the applicable regulatory and contractual framework.
Upholding the Bombay High Court's decision, the Supreme Court held that the Administrator's action was impermissible.
The appeals were accordingly dismissed.
The Court further clarified that the annual coupon payments would remain unaffected by the outcome of the appeals and must be made in accordance with the Information Memoranda.
Dua Associates represented ECL Finance Limited, Respondent No. 14, before the Supreme Court.

stories.title: Delhi SIR : Why Deleted Voters Asked To File Form 6 When They Were On 2026 Rolls? Supreme Court Asks ECI
stories.summary: The ECI agreed to consider allowing shifted voters to file enumeration forms or Form 8.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The ECI agreed to consider allowing shifted voters to file enumeration forms or Form 8.

With respect to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Delhi, the Supreme Court on Wednesday questioned the Election Commission of India over asking persons deleted from the draft roll for not filling up enumeration forms to use Form 6 to register as new voters, when they were on the 2026 rolls.
The Court pointed out that Form 6 is meant for first-time voters, where the applicants have to declare that they have not voted before.
The Court underscored that in Delhi, there would be various persons on whom enumeration forms could not be served as they changed their addresses, or have temporarily gone out of the city for work.
Why cannot they be given an opportunity to fill enumeration forms or file Form 8(to show change in address), instead of filing Form 6, the Court asked.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing the writ petition filed by Anjali Bharadwaj and Amrita Johri raising issues regarding the Delhi SIR process.
Responding to the concerns flagged by the bench, Senior Advocate Dama Seshadri Naidu, for the ECI, said that the authorities will examine them and take remedial steps.
Naidu also said that the ECI will consider extending the deadline.
The bench suggested creating a residual category to deal with persons who have temporarily shifted.
Advocate Prashant Bhushan, for the petitioners, submitted that out of 47 lakh deleted voters, 43 lakhs are shown to be permanently shifted or absent.
Bhushan said that these are persons who never received enumeration forms.
But the ECI is not allowing them to file Form 8 (to alter address), and asking to file Form 6.
